newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds aid to Hualon textiles plant in Belfast.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds aid to Hualon textiles plant in Belfast.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed on Thursday an appeal from British and Belgian textile companies against a Commission decision to allow aid to set up a textile plant in Northern Ireland.
The British government received the Commission's approval to grant 61 million pounds in aid to the newly created Hualon Corporation for its textile plant in Belfast in 1994.
Hualon is owned by the Taiwanese based Hualon Group which produces synthetic fibers, primarily polyamide.

The arguments against the aid were raised by Apparel, Knitting & Textiles (AKT) of England and the Association Internationale des Utilisateurs de Fils de Filaments Artificiels et Synthetiques et de Soie Naturelle (AIUFFASS) of Belgium.
AKT and AIUFFASS, as well as member states submitting opinions, raised issues of excess capacity and stagnating demand for textiles in the Community at the time the aid was granted.
The court said in order to justify overturning the Commission's decision, it must find the Commission committed a manifest error assessing facts at the time it granted the aid.
In order for that threshold to be established, the challenging parties must put up sufficient evidence to show the facts used by the Commission led to an implausible conclusion.

Instead, the court found the complaint unfounded, and agreed the aid was properly granted under the exception to competition rules allowed in EC article 92(3)(a) and (c) which permits regional aid to promote economic development.
EXCERPTS TO THE JUDGMENT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Action for annulment - State aid - Textiles - Trade association - Admissibility - Manifest error of assessment - Excess capacity"
Case T-380/94
Association Internationale des Utilisateurs de Fils de Filaments Artificiels et Synthetiques et de Soie Naturelle (AIUFFASS)
Apparel, Knitting & Textiles Alliance (AKT), applicants
v
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
supported by
United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, intervener

application for annulment of the Commission decision of 31 May 1994, reproduced in Commission Notice 94/C 271/06, authorizing the Government of the United Kingdom under article 92(3)(a) and (c) of the EC Treaty to grant aid of 61 million pounds sterling in favour of Hualon Corporation for the setting up of a textile producing plant in Northern Ireland (OJ 1994 C 271, p. 5)
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
1. Dismisses the application;
2. Orders the applicants to bear their own costs and jointly and severally to pay the Commission's costs;
3. Orders the United Kingdom to ear its own costs.
